In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Munafiqun

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say, "We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah." And Allah knows that you are His Messenger, and Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are liars.﴾

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, said in the study notes: The address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), and "al-munafiqun" is the plural of "munafiq" (hypocrite), who is one who displays faith and conceals disbelief.

﴿They say, "We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah"﴾, i.e., they said that out of hypocrisy and fear, and they did not say it sincerely from their hearts. Therefore Allah said: ﴿And Allah knows that you are His Messenger, and Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are liars.﴾ He bore witness against them with lying even though the outward of their words was true, because their inner states contradict their outward appearances, since actions are by intentions. The alif of "inna" is kasra in the three places because it follows a verb suspended by the lam (al-lam al-mu'allaqah); were it not so, it would be fath, since it would be in the position of a verbal noun (masdar).

Abu Hayyan has a fine statement on this, when he said: Their saying "nashhadu" (we bear witness) functions as an oath, and for this reason it is followed by what follows an oath; likewise the verb of certainty, and "knowing" functions as an oath with His saying: ﴿Indeed you are the Messenger of Allah﴾, meaning with the intent of emphasis by "inna" and the lam. Then he said: The essence of testimony is that the tongue agrees with the heart; the former is by utterance and the latter by belief. So Allah refuted them and exposed them with His saying: ﴿And Allah knows that you are His Messenger, and Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are liars.﴾

That is: their hearts did not agree with their tongues in confirming you, and their belief was that you are not a messenger. So they are liars in the sight of Allah and in the sight of whoever knows their state; or they are liars in their own selves, since they believe that their statement "You are indeed the Messenger of Allah" is a lie.

The saying of the Exalted, ﴿And Allah knows that you are His Messenger﴾, came between their testimony and their denial, as a notification that the matter is as they said, in the manner of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And sufficient is Allah as a witness. Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah﴾ [al-Fath: 28-29].

Note

(p-189) In this verse there is a rhetorical discussion on the division of speech into khabar (informative speech) and insha' (performative speech). They said: khabar is that which admits of truth and falsehood in itself. The majority held that it is confined to these two without intermediary, and the one informing is either truthful or lying; this is based on the correspondence of the report to reality or its non-correspondence, and it has no connection to belief.

As-Sa'd said in at-Talkhis: Some people said: the truth and falsehood of a report is its correspondence to the belief of the reporter, not to reality, and they argued for that by saying that non-correspondence to reality is a mistake, not a lie.

And the hadith of Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, from Ibn Umar: "He did not lie, but he made a mistake." This is the view of al-Jahiz, namely that the truth of a report is its correspondence to reality together with the belief of the reporter, arguing from the verse: ﴿And Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are liars﴾, together with their saying: ﴿You are indeed the Messenger of Allah﴾. So Allah called them liars although their report corresponded to reality, but they did not believe what they said, so Allah called them liars for that.

The consequence of al-Jahiz's view is affirming an intermediary between truth and falsehood, namely the reporter's not believing what he reports, even if it corresponds to reality. But what we have already mentioned from the words of Abu Hayyan refutes this view and invalidates al-Jahiz's argument and that of those who agree with him from the verse, because Allah's calling them liars is directed at their saying "we bear witness," and testimony is more specific than report. Also, they included in their testimony emphasis that implies an oath and suggests the agreement of the saying with what is in the heart, especially in this context, which is the context of faith and affirmation. So Allah called them liars regarding their report, in the form of testimony and state, in that they did not bring testimony in its proper manner, which is its non-agreement with their belief.

The Qur'an negates an intermediary between truth and falsehood, as in His saying: ﴿So what is there after the truth but error?﴾ [Yunus: 32].

As for the jurisprudence of oaths, what they are concluded by, and their rulings, the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, has already treated this topic in full in Surah al-Ma'idah at His saying: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 89] and what follows.

(p-190) Regarding the meaning of laghw al-yamin (unintentional oath) among the scholars there are two views:

The second of them: it is that one swears to what he believes, but it turns out to be other than what he believes. He attributed this to Malik, and said it is narrated from Aisha, Abu Hurayrah, and Ibn Abbas in one of his two views, and he listed many names. It is not far-fetched to say: one should distinguish between the linguistic definition among the rhetoricians and the legal definition, where what is based on the speaker's strong presumption is legally accepted, since it is the limit of his knowledge, and because there is no blame in the Shari'ah for such a case. And Allah knows best.

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

(p-417) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Munafiqun

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say, "We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah"﴾ — the verse.

What they testified to is true, because the message of our Prophet (ﷺ) is true without doubt. Allah refuted them with His saying: ﴿And Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are liars﴾ [63]. Yet His saying: ﴿And Allah knows that you are His Messenger﴾ [63] seems like an affirmation of them.

The answer is that His refutation of them is directed at their attributing the testimony to themselves in their saying "we bear witness," while in the inner reality they do not testify to his message; rather they believe it is false, or they doubt it, as the first is indicated by His saying about them: ﴿Shall we believe as the fools have believed?﴾ — up to His saying — ﴿but they do not know﴾ [al-Baqarah: 13]. And the second is indicated by His saying: ﴿Their hearts are in doubt, so they wander in their doubt﴾ [al-Tawbah: 45].

**Verse 63:2: "They have taken their oaths as a shield"**

Al-Shinqiti's words: "His saying, Most High: ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield﴾."

The word *أيمانهم* ("their oaths") is read with a *fatha* on the hamza, as the plural of *yamin* (oath, right hand). It is also read with a *kasra* on the hamza, from *al-iman* (faith), the opposite of *kufr* (disbelief). On this reading the meaning is: what they displayed of the matters of Islam.

What has preceded is that among the types of *bayan* (the science of clarifying meaning) is the case where a verse has two readings, and one of them is given preference by other evidence. Abu Hayyan's discussion has already been cited, in which he takes the word as referring to oaths.

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, says in *Mudhakkirat al-Tadris* (a reference work by al-Shinqiti): *al-Ayman* is the plural of *yamin*, which means the oath. *Al-junnah* is the *turs*, which is the *mijann*, the shield with which swords, arrows and missiles are warded off in battle. The meaning is that when some of the hypocrites' hypocrisy becomes apparent, or a word of disbelief is heard from them, they swear by Allah that they did not say or do that. They make their oath a shield that protects them from the Prophet's (ﷺ) holding them accountable for their sin. As Allah, Most High, says: ﴿They swear by Allah that they did not say it, but they did say the word of disbelief﴾ [At-Tawbah 9:74]. He also says: ﴿They swear by Allah that they are indeed among you, but they are not of you﴾ [At-Tawbah 9:56]. And He says: ﴿They swear by Allah to you in order to please you﴾ [At-Tawbah 9:62], and similar verses. These texts show that they swear oaths upon their oaths.

From the perspective of meaning: their oaths and swearing are directed at the claim of their faith. There is no separation between the oath and the faith, because they swear that they are believers. The oath is more specific than faith, and taking the general term to mean the more specific one implies the existence of the broader. So swearing upon faith entails the claim of faith plus something more, whereas the mere claim of faith does not entail emphasis by swearing and oath-taking.

**Verse 63:2: "So they barred [others] from the way of Allah"**

Al-Shinqiti's words: "His saying, Most High: ﴿So they barred [others] from the way of Allah﴾."

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, says: That is, because they took their oaths as a shield and their inner disbelief was concealed, they were able to bar some people from the way of Allah. This is because the Muslims thought them to be brothers when they were enemies, and the worst enemy is the one you think to be a friend. For this reason Allah warned His Prophet about them, saying: ﴿They are the enemy, so beware of them﴾ [Al-Munafiqun 63:4]. Their barring people from the way of Allah is like their hindering them from jihad, as He explained in His saying: ﴿Allah already knows those among you who hinder others, and those who say to their brothers, "Come to us"﴾ [Al-Ahzab 33:18], and His saying: ﴿They said, "Do not march out in the heat"﴾ [At-Tawbah 9:81], and His saying: ﴿Those who said of their brothers, while they themselves sat back, "If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed"﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:168].

**Verse 63:2: "Indeed, evil is what they used to do"**

Al-Shinqiti's words: "His saying, Most High: ﴿Indeed, evil is what they used to do﴾."

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, says: *Saa'* (ساء, "evil/was evil") is a rigid verb used to express censure, with the meaning of *bi'sa* (بئس, "wretched was"). End of quote.

Allah, Most High, has clarified that evil conduct of the hypocrites in several respects, among them His saying: ﴿They deceive Allah and those who believe﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:9], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites try to deceive Allah, but He is the one who deceives them﴾ [An-Nisa' 4:142].

Their deceit was by speech and by action. Their deceit by speech is in His saying about them: ﴿They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts﴾ [Al-Fath 48:11]. Their deceit by action is in His saying about them: ﴿When they stand up to pray, they stand lazily, showing off to people﴾ [An-Nisa' 4:142]. And in jihad, there is their saying: ﴿Indeed, our homes are exposed," though they were not exposed. They only wanted to flee﴾ [Al-Ahzab 33:13].

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah al-Munafiqun (63), verse 3:**

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿That is because they believed and then disbelieved, so a seal was set upon their hearts.﴾

In this verse there is a clear statement that the sealing upon their hearts is a consequence of their disbelief after their belief. Similar to it is His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Rather, Allah has sealed it over because of their disbelief.﴾ (Surat al-Nisa', 155). And like His statement: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate.﴾ (Surat al-Saff, 5).

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, said, concerning some of the scholars: "That is because they believed," i.e., with their tongues, hypocritically, "then they disbelieved," with their hearts, in reality. End of quotation.

It has preceded in the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿Allah has sealed their hearts﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah, 7), so they do not understand after this sealing. And along with this sealing is His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it.﴾ (Surat al-Kahf, 57).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 63, verse 4:

Allah's statement: ﴿They are the enemy, so beware of them.﴾

In it there is something that suggests the restriction of enmity to the hypocrites, even though enmity also exists among the polytheists and the Jews. However, the polytheists' open display of their polytheism and the Jews' proclaiming of their disbelief are naturally a cause for caution.

As for these (the hypocrites), their claim of faith and their swearing to it may suggest that one should lean toward them, even if only out of a desire to win them over. Therefore they were more deserving of warning against than the others, because of the severity of their enmity and the strength of their mixing with the Muslims, which enables them to gain knowledge of all the Muslims' affairs.

And it has come at the end of the whole surah, revealing their true nature and clarifying the severity of their enmity, both in their saying: ﴿Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 7], and in their plotting against the Muslims in their saying: ﴿If we return to Madinah, the mightier will surely expel the weaker therefrom﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 8], and His statement: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 6].

(Hum) here refers to the hypocrites, as in His statement: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites are the defiantly disobedient﴾ [al-Tawbah: 67].

The author said in (Dafʿ Ihām al-Iḍṭirāb ʿan Āyāt al-Kitāb):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them﴾, and the verse [continues].

The apparent meaning of this noble verse is that the hypocrites will not be forgiven under any circumstances. Yet there is another verse which gives the impression that there is hope of their being forgiven if the Messenger (ﷺ) asks forgiveness for them more than seventy times, namely Allah the Exalted's saying: ﴿Even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will never forgive them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 80].

The answer is that this last verse makes clear that they will not be forgiven in any case, because they are disbelievers inwardly.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And to Allah belongs the treasures of the heavens and the earth﴾.

Its explanation has already preceded, from the Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth﴾ [az-Zumar: 63].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 63, verse 8:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿They say, "If we return to Al-Madinah, the more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble." But honor belongs to Allah, and to His Messenger, and to the believers.﴾

It has already preceded from the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, an explanation of what this verse contains of al-Qawl bil-Muwjab (the speech of "according to what is implied," i.e., turning an opponent's own premise against him).

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 63, verse 9:**

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿O you who have believed, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah.﴾

[p. 193] The discussion of this was already given by the Shaykh (may Allah have mercy on him and on us) at the verse: ﴿Wealth and children are the adornment of the worldly life﴾ [al-Kahf: 46]. He explained the reason why wealth and children divert one from the remembrance of Allah, namely that the servant is tested through them, as Allah says in the verse that comes later in the surah "al-Taghabun" (Mutual Loss and Gain): ﴿Your wealth and your children are only a trial, and Allah has with Him a great reward﴾ [al-Taghabun: 15].

That is, [the warning applies] to one who devotes wealth to obedience to Allah. On reflection on the end of this surah and the end of the one before it, we find a unity of theme and direction.

There is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And when they see a transaction or a diversion, they rush toward it and leave you standing. Say: What is with Allah is better than diversion and than transaction, and Allah is the best of providers﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 11].

Immediately after it comes the surah: ﴿When the hypocrites come to you﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 1]. Perhaps this indicates that those who hastened to go out to the caravan were the hypocrites, and the others followed them because of their need for what the caravan carried. Here, after the hypocrites inclined toward wealth, there came: ﴿Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse﴾. Thus their wealth became a trial for them in that statement of theirs. Allah then warned the believers with His saying: ﴿Let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah﴾, whether the intended meaning of "wealth" is specifically the matter of the sermon and the caravan mentioned earlier, or the general sense of acts of worship and means of livelihood.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 63, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And spend of what We have provided for you﴾.

In it is spending from part of what He has provided them. The discussion of moderation (iqtisad) in spending (infaq) has already been presented by the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon him and upon us, at His saying at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿And from what We have provided them they spend﴾ [al-Baqarah: 3].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 63, verse 11:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah will never delay a soul when its appointed time has come.﴾

Likewise He does not bring it forward before it. As in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿For every nation there is an appointed term. When their term comes, they cannot delay it by an hour, nor can they advance it.﴾ [Yunus: 49].

He, may He be exalted, made clear that they will not be delayed, although they were promised that they would give charity and be among the righteous, pointing to the cause in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah is Aware of what you do﴾ [al-Taghabun: 11], meaning: even if He were to delay you, because your nature is lying and breaking promises, and this is the habit of their likes, as He made clear in His saying: ﴿And warn mankind of the Day when the punishment will come to them, and those who wronged will say, "Our Lord, delay us for a near term; we will answer Your call and follow the messengers." Had you not previously sworn that you would have no decline?﴾ (p-194) [Ibrahim: 44].

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿[Until, when death comes to one of them, he says, "My Lord, send me back, that I may do righteousness in what I have left behind." No! It is only a word he is saying.﴾] [al-Mu'minun: 99-100].

His saying, may He be exalted, concerning them: ﴿No! It is only a word he is saying,﴾ is equivalent in its truthfulness.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah is Aware of what you do.﴾

Meaning: even if He were to delay them, they would not be truthful, and they would not be among the righteous. Allah, may He be exalted, has encompassing knowledge of what will be, just as He encompasses what has been. And Allah, may He be exalted, knows best.
